edits.why: version statement: the tutorial now targets NumPy 2.5

edits.old: We start with a float array of random integers, cast with `np.float`.
edits.new: We start with a float array of random integers, cast with `float`.
edits.why: np.float alias was removed; the builtin float is the replacement

edits.old: Column products come from `np.product`, which multiplies along an axis.
edits.new: Column products come from `np.prod`, which multiplies along an axis.
edits.why: np.product was removed in favour of np.prod

edits.old: `np.cumproduct` gives running products of a list.
edits.new: `np.cumprod` gives running products of a list.
edits.why: np.cumproduct was removed in favour of np.cumprod
np.NaN was removed; the lowercase np.nan is the name

edits.old: Column means were checked on NumPy 1.21.
edits.new: Column means were checked on NumPy 2.5.
edits.why: version statement: the tutorial now targets NumPy 2.5

edits.old: Sort scores stored as `np.float_` values and keep the order with `np.argsort`.
edits.new: Sort scores stored as `np.float64` values and keep the order with `np.argsort`.
edits.why: np.float_ was removed; np.float64 is the explicit dtype
